messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Analysis The sentence is an archaic moral plea in which the speaker urges the listener to consider both the speaker's condition and the father's suffering. It asks whether the speaker should abandon a blind, destitute father struggling with infirmity and poverty, especially when the speaker has the power to fill his later years with comfort and joy. Analysis
Structure The semicolon joins two imperatives, Consydre thou myne condicyon and reflecte upon myne fader, creating a direct appeal to conscience. The rhetorical question then expands into a long conditional sequence that contrasts forsaking the father with providing him comfort, using repeated when clauses to heighten the ethical urgency. Structure
Meaning The core meaning is that duty to a parent outweighs self interest, because the father is vulnerable and the speaker is able to relieve his suffering. The archaic spelling and grammar intensify solemnity, while the contrast between penury and joy makes the moral choice vivid. Meaning
